name: Submission To Human Authority
overview: Scripture teaches that believers are called to submit to human authorities because such powers are established by God, as Romans 13:1 emphasizes. This submission is expressed through obedience to magistrates and readiness to do good, as instructed in Titus 3:1 and Hebrews 13:17, recognizing that leaders have a spiritual responsibility to care for their people. However, this submission is not absolute; Acts 5:29 clarifies that obedience to God takes precedence when human commands conflict with divine commands. Jesus' teaching in Matthew 22:21 further distinguishes the roles of earthly authorities and God, underscoring the believer's ultimate allegiance to God while respecting civil responsibilities. Ephesians 5:21 encourages mutual submission among believers, motivated by reverence for God, framing submission as a relational and God-honoring practice.
